idea_name: Fitness-decay triggered walk-forward re-optimization as regime-adaptation sensor
mechanism: Live EA periodically (every InpBarsReOptimize bars, or when trading KPIs fall to a critical level) re-runs a population optimizer on a rolling history window of InpBarsOptimize bars via a virtualized copy of the strategy (virtual Stochastic + VirtualStrategy). Best parameter set replaces live Set[]; re-opt events themselves mark adaptation to changed conditions. Fitness can be balance, PF, expectancy, or an integral/cumulative criterion sampled at many history points.
data_needed: Rolling OHLC CopyRates window; virtualized indicator buffers; fitness series on virtual trades; re-opt bar clock and optional KPI threshold
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol PERIOD_CURRENT; demo Stochastic EA (K period, upper/lower levels); InpBarsOptimize=18000, InpBarsReOptimize=1440; 1-year tester comparison with/without SelfOptimization
why_new_for_mis: Treats scheduled or KPI-triggered re-optimization as an explicit regime-change response channel—MIS can log fitness decay and re-opt timestamps as sensors that market conditions have invalidated the current parameter sleeve.
quote: The re-optimization point can be chosen for various reasons. It can be a strictly defined number of history bars, as in the example below, or some specific condition, for example, a decrease in trading indicators to a certain critical level.

quote: Optimization algorithms can be used to rank assets based on various criteria such as profitability, volatility or liquidity.

mechanism: Implements C_AO / C_AO_Agent inheritance, utilities, selectable test functions (Ackley, Goldstein-Price, Shaffer #2, discrete Skin/Hilly), and a unified C_TestStand. Mentions ANN-adaptive AO hybrids only as future research directions, not as market sensors.

idea_name: RNG quality vs AO search efficiency
mechanism: Chi-square uniformity tests of MQL5 std RNG vs Mersenne Twister64; BGA and (P_O)ES runs on 50 Hilly functions show negligible fitness gain from better RNG at ~3.5× slower generation. No market sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic Hilly test functions; BGA and (P_O)ES algorithms
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—RNG quality for optimizers only.
quote: The preliminary conclusion is this: the quality of random number generators does not affect the performance of optimization algorithms.

idea_name: Grid fill-depth and breakeven distance as adverse-excursion sensor
mechanism: Derive closed-form breakeven b(x), take-profit level t(x), cycle profit p(x) and ruin cost c(x) for a geometric lot-multiplier grid of x orders spaced by Distance D (floor-adjusted for lot rounding). Live or simulated x (orders filled before TP vs ruin) and b(x) distance below B1 quantify how far price ran against the book—an adverse-excursion / move-intensity reading. Notes TP vs ruin probabilities require price-data simulation (next parts).
data_needed: Grid params IP, IL, D, M, N/x, TP, static spread S; price path for hit probabilities; realized order count per cycle
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD preferred (lower volatility); pip-distance D; Python simulation of p(x)/c(x) for x=1..20; Part IV math only
why_new_for_mis: Turns realized grid depth and analytical breakeven distance into a market adverse-move intensity sensor MIS can track without a separate vol model.
quote: To account for probabilities, we need price data and coding-based optimization rather than just equations, which we will explore in further parts of the series.

idea_name: STF dual demand/supply MLP forecast of bullishness vs bearishness
mechanism: Two MLPs: demand f_x(x_v(t), G_v(t), δt) with inputs [day-of-week T, spatial G, High−Open]; supply f_y(x_v, y_v, G_v, δt) with inputs [T, G, High−Open, Open−Low]. Softplus MLP (~3/5/1 and 4/5/1), online train ~250–10000 epochs at lr 0.5. Signal = demand_forecast − supply_forecast (positive→bullish). Positions held until signal reverses.
data_needed: OHLC series; train_set length; day-of-week index; G determinant; dual network weights/biases
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_D1 year 2023; notes H4/H1 possible with denser time indices (e.g. fifteen 8h bars/week)
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a dual-objective neural sensor that separately forecasts upside and downside range pressure then nets them—richer than single-target price prediction for regime-aware signals.
quote: by subtracting supply model output from demand output we a double number whose positive value would indicate bullishness and whose negative value would mean bearishness.

idea_name: High-Open / Open-Low as upward/downward volatility proxy buffers
mechanism: Demand buffer = high−open (≥0; zero ⇒ hangman/flat); supply buffer = open−low (≥0; zero ⇒ gravestone/flat). Used as volume-of-bullish/bearish-contracts proxies when real long/short volume is unavailable in FX, and as the dual timeseries targets/inputs for STF forecasting.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 in tests; applicable to any OHLC symbol/TF
why_new_for_mis: Defines a clean signed-range volatility pair MIS can stream as separate up-vol and down-vol channels without depending on broker volume.
quote: the high prices less the open prices are chosen as an alternative buffer to real long volume contracts... meant to measure upward volatility

idea_name: Split-window High/Low correlation determinant as spatial G sensor
mechanism: Build 2×2 matrix from first/second halves of length-2*m_train_set High (X) and Low (Y) vectors: m00=corr(x1,x2), m01=corr(x1,y2), m10=corr(y1,x2), m11=corr(y1,y2); feed det(m) as the spatial G input to both demand and supply networks (optionally feed all four cells instead).
data_needed: Two consecutive m_train_set windows of High and Low series
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; CopyRates mode 2 (high) and 4 (low); train_set hyperparameter
why_new_for_mis: Compresses cross- and auto-structure of high/low ranges into a single spatial coordinate for sequence models—MIS can use G (or the full matrix) as a microstructure/regime-shape feature.
quote: metadata for our bullish and bearish price buffers will be got from the correlation readings shared by these buffers... we stuck to the determinant

idea_name: Day-of-week temporal index as STF time channel
mechanism: Map bar datetime to a compact weekday index T∈{0..4} (Mon=0 default, Tue=1…Fri/Sat=4) and feed T as the temporal input of both demand and supply networks. For sub-daily TFs, replace with intra-week bar index (e.g. fifteen 8h slots) or session/hour index.
data_needed: Bar open time → MqlDateTime.day_of_week (or custom intra-week index)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 primary; article discusses 8h/H4/H1 alternatives
why_new_for_mis: Provides a lightweight calendar/time embedding for neural sensors so MIS forecasts can condition on weekday/session structure without a full calendar model.
quote: Testing which is covered in the next section will be done on the daily time frame so the week of day index does easily tie into that.

quote: Numba has been shown to provide the 50x speed boost. Testing becomes fast, allowing for multiple tests and even parameter optimization.
